title: Session-aware rate partitioning and eviction safeguard for dedicated pools
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Implement a session-aware admission layer for Dedicated pools that partitions tenant throughput across active sessions, provides hard/soft throughput guarantees, and adds an eviction safeguard to prevent high churn or infinite queue growth during overload.

Motivation: Some customers run many concurrent short-lived sessions (chat windows, interactive tools). Current per-tenant rate limits do not distinguish session-local hotspots, leading to noisy neighbour effects inside a tenant: a few aggressive sessions consume shared tenant quota and force other sessions into the slowpath or shedding. We need: 1) deterministic per-session partitioning tied to a tenant's committed throughput; 2) a soft eviction policy that prefers dropping the most wasteful queued work (stale sessions, long-idle requests) and 3) signal plumbing to the autoscaler to adjust headroom when session concurrency spikes.

Core components and behavior:
- Session Partitioning: assign each active session a transient weight derived from (session_activity_score, session_age, tenant_priority). Weight normalization ensures sum(weights) <= tenant_committed_qps + tenant_burst_credits.
- Minimum Session Floor: reserve a tiny guaranteed token bucket for every newly created session for bounding cold-start latency (configurable floor).
- Soft Eviction Safeguard: when queue depth > threshold or predicted wait > SLO, run a lightweight scoring function to evict/abort queued requests from sessions with low utility (e.g., long idle, repeated cancellations, >99th percentile cost per token). Eviction decisions are logged and emitted as metrics for audit/review.
- Backpressure Feedback: produce per-tenant and per-session headroom metrics that feed the autoscaler hints endpoint. Autoscaler uses exponential-weighted headroom trends to pre-scale dedicated pools instead of reactive cold-scaling.
- Graceful Fallback: when committed capacity is saturated, lower-priority sessions are throttled into deferred-execution (deferred slots) with a best-effort retry window; critical sessions may fallback to alternate model variants with lower cost per token.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit and integration tests for partitioning math, floor guarantees, and eviction ordering.
- Load test demonstrating improved fairness across sessions for a synthetic tenant with 200 concurrent sessions (latency P95 improves for median sessions by >=20% under same tenant load).
- Autoscaler reacts to headroom signals and completes scale-up within target lead (configured at 30s for hot-path).
- Telemetry dashboards with eviction counts, per-session headroom, and per-tenant fairness index.

Non-goals: cross-tenant fairness (still enforced by higher-level tenant quotas), replacing existing global admission shard.

Implementation notes: prefer a mostly lock-free algorithm for scoring to avoid CPU amplification during spikes; implement eviction selectors as pluggable strategies for experimentation.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Ava Martinez: Created ticket after incident where a single bot-driven session in customer X consumed tenant quota and caused user-facing degradations. Logged initial design hypothesis and performance goals.

2026-02-27 - Liam Chen: Spike complete. Implemented prototype of session weight calc in go/admission/session_partition.go. Prototype uses activity_score = recent_tokens * decay + recency_bonus. Results from localbench: fairness improved but CPU overhead increased by ~7%.
2026-03-02 - Design review (Sofia Patel): Suggested UI signals in Console for session-level throttles and a way to whitelist sessions for debug. Added 'eviction_audit' metric requirement.

2026-03-05 - Security review (internal): Confirmed no new customer data is persisted; session ids are hashed before logs. Security team requested KMS flag gating for any persisted debug traces. Marked for follow-up but not blocking.

2026-03-08 - Engineering sync: Decided to implement the eviction scorer as a two-pass filter - cheap heuristics first, expensive scoring second (to bound CPU). Also agreed to expose autoscaler hint via existing '/autoscaler/hints' push endpoint.
2026-03-10 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/11452 - session-partitioning: core admission path and headroom signal tests. Requesting review from @ravi and @meera.

2026-03-11 - Load test: k8s e2e run w/ tc-netem to simulate network jitter. Observed median latency improvement for non-aggressive sessions: 24%. Eviction rate stable at 0.6% of requests in worst-case run. Need to tune floor_size to reduce small-session cold-start failures.
2026-03-12 - Next steps: finalize PR feedback, add Console signal widgets (PM: Noor). Coordinate with autoscaler team for integration smoke test in staging next week.
